claim: Veurne's Boetprocessie (Procession of the Penitents) takes place on the last Sunday of July each year, with the 2026 edition on Sunday 26 July; hooded penitents walk barefoot carrying heavy wooden crosses through the historic centre.
quote: The annual Boeteprocessie (procession of the penitents) takes place every year on the last Sunday of July ... Penitents in coarse robes and hoods walk barefoot through town, many carrying heavy wooden crosses.

claim: Veurne's Sint-Walburga church is an exceptional example of Scheldt Gothic architecture rising from the centre of town, with origins in the 12th century and a Gothic choir completed in the early 14th century.
quote: Sint-Walburga Church is an exceptional example of Scheldt Gothic architecture and one of Belgium's most remarkable religious buildings. Rising from the centre of Veurne, it stands as a witness to nearly a millennium of history.

claim: Veurne holds a weekly market on the Grote Markt every Wednesday from 8:00 to 13:00 with flowers, textiles, vegetables, fruit and dairy.
quote: Elke woensdag vindt van 8u tot 13u op de Grote Markt de wekelijkse markt plaats ... bloemen, textiel, groenten en fruit tot zuivel.

claim: Nieuwpoort's Stadshalle and 35-metre belfry on the market square is a UNESCO-listed late-Gothic belfry, dynamited in WWI and reconstructed 1921-1923 to its medieval appearance.
quote: Above the Stadshalle rises the square, late-Gothic belfry tower of 35 meters high ... During World War I, the tower was dynamited ... In 1921-1923, the belfry and hall were reconstructed according to the historical model.

claim: Nieuwpoort's Vismijn (fish auction hall) on the IJzer hosts wholesale fish auctions starting 07:00-08:00 on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, viewable in person or by guided tour.
quote: Trawlers unload their catch for daily wholesale auctions beginning at 07:00 or 08:00, and you can watch these in person on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, or sign up for a guided tour.

claim: Diksmuide's 84-metre IJzertoren is Flanders' foremost nationalist peace symbol, with 22 floors of WWI and Flemish emancipation museum content and an open-air viewing platform.
quote: this colossal 84m-high 'peace' tower is at once crushingly ugly and fascinating. The tower is probably Flanders' foremost nationalist symbol: its 22 floors house a very expansive museum related to WWI and Flemish emancipation.

claim: Diksmuide's Sint-Niklaaskerk anchors the Grote Markt and was rebuilt in elaborate Gothic style after near-total destruction in WWI, with a climbable 13th-century tower offering summer views.
quote: The church was almost completely destroyed in WWI but was rebuilt in its elaborate Gothic style soon afterwards on the same site. Behind the Grote Markt's southeast corner, St-Niklaaskerk has a bulky 13th-century tower that you can climb for good summer views.

claim: Koksijde's Ten Duinen Abbey was a wealthy medieval Cistercian monastery (community founded 1107, Cistercian from 1139) whose ruins were buried in dunes and excavated from 1949; the site is now an open-air archaeological museum.
quote: Ten Duinen Abbey (the Abbey of the Dunes) was a Cistercian monastery at Koksijde ... A religious community was founded in the dunes near Koksijde by the hermit Ligerius in 1107, and in 1139 it became affiliated to the Cistercian Order.

claim: Koksijde's Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-ter-Duinenkerk (1956-1965) by Jozef Lantsoght has a cockle-shell floor plan and is one of the most progressive post-war church buildings in Flanders, protected as a monument since 2005, nicknamed a 'cathedral of light'.
quote: Het grondplan van deze moderne kerk is geïnspireerd op de kokkel ... Sinds 2005 is het gebouw beschermd als monument en kan beschouwd worden als een van de meest opvallende en meest progressieve naoorlogse kerkgebouwen in Vlaanderen.

claim: The Abdijmuseum Ten Duinen in Koksijde is the main heritage attraction of the dunes village, presenting the Cistercian abbey's history alongside the visible archaeological foundations.
De Panne to Veurne is about 5.7 km direct (8 km by road), with a 7-minute train or 14-minute bus connection; the four historic towns are all within 25 km / 30 minutes' drive of De Panne.
quote: The distance between De Panne and Veurne is 5.7 km ... The road distance is 8 km ... The fastest train journey is 7 minutes.

claim: De Panne to Koksijde is a short coastal drive of roughly 6 miles / ~11 minutes, making Koksijde the closest of the four historic towns to Subtiel.
